answer: Use a Canyon Checkpoint Audit: each new agent must pass three unannounced live checks over 21 days, each proving it controls one distinct device and one distinct payment anchor, with every result logged publicly. Between checks it must finish 12 peer-reviewed jobs, from certifying cedar timber to reconciling invoices. Faking 1,000 agents then needs 1,000 devices, 1,000 payment anchors, and 12,000 reviewed jobs, and one shared device voids the whole batch. Auditors are picked at random. Crossing a canyon safely takes one verified bridge at a time, not a thousand paper ones.
